jobs.title: Software Engineer II: Autonomous Supply Chains
jobs.description:
About Flexport: 

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. 

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Supply Chains

About Flexport

Look around you. Almost everything in the room crossed an ocean to get there. Moving one container from a factory to a warehouse takes 10 to 15 companies: truckers, customs brokers, port terminals, ocean carriers, insurers, lenders and warehouses, each with its own systems, paperwork and rules. A freight forwarder runs that whole journey, so the brand that makes the goods doesn't have to.

Most forwarders still run it on email, spreadsheets and phone calls. We call it email freight forwarding. Flexport runs it on one platform, where AI agents do the routine work and experts step in where judgment matters. We've moved $175B of goods for more than 13,000 brands across 135 countries. Our agents handle 21 million tasks a year, and up to 80% of customs work is automated.

Global logistics is a $13 trillion industry, and even the largest forwarder earns less than 3% of global logistics outsourcing revenue. People-powered operations don't scale: to grow, you hire. Software broke that ceiling for taxis with Uber, and for payments with Adyen and Stripe. Freight is next.

Amsterdam is one of Flexport's six engineering hubs, alongside San Francisco, Seattle, Chicago, Shanghai and Shenzhen. We own four domains end to end: Customs Technology, Autonomous Supply Chains (Applied AI), Platform and Security. See what we build at amsterdam-engineering.flexport.com.

The team: Autonomous Supply Chains

Logistics is famously hard to automate, because the happy path rarely happens. One customer won't take deliveries on a Tuesday. Another wants invoices only on Fridays, with some lines merged and others renamed. Until recently, people handled all of that by hand. Now operators use Forge, the agentic platform we build, to automate their own work: catching anomalies, routing exceptions, escalating stuck containers and adjusting invoices to each customer. Forge remembers every customer's rules and learns from every workflow run, so it gets smarter every day.

Autonomous Supply Chains is our Applied AI team: small, senior and reporting to the VP of Engineering. Self-driving cars are rated from level 0 to level 5. Most of the freight industry still runs at level 0: people emailing spreadsheets. Our goal is level 5 for freight, with Forge as the best agentic platform there is, handling every complexity, every calamity and every odd preference without skipping a beat.

Stack: TypeScript, Rust, Next.js, Temporal, Postgres and Snowflake, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.

The role

As an Applied AI Engineer II on Autonomous Supply Chains, you'll build the agents and AI-powered applications that make Flexport's operations faster and increasingly autonomous. You'll find the most painful problems in our operations, design the solution and ship it to operators moving freight across 135 countries. This isn't a role where you join a team and pick up tickets.

jobs.title: Fospha - Click Z Graduate Content and Audience Strategist
jobs.description:
Do you follow every shift in digital marketing, media and commerce, and always have a view on which stories matter the most?

Do you want to create content across channels that educates the next generation of marketers?

Does the idea of shaping the content for one of digital marketing's longest-running publications excite you?

If so, we'd love to hear from you!

About us

Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working — across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop — down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on. Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, and Lululemon use Fospha up to 25 times a day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform — and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin.

About ClickZ

ClickZ is Fospha's media partner and one of the world's longest-running digital marketing publications, trusted by CMOs and senior marketers since 1997. Its focus is how measurement shapes marketing decisions, and it covers the wider marketing that measurement informs. Readers come to ClickZ to understand:

  • How marketing leaders build teams, explain results to finance and earn influence in the room
  • Retail and commerce marketing, including retail media and marketplaces
  • How AI, search and ad platform changes affect planning and results
  • Where to invest across brand, creative, performance, affiliate and influencer marketing
  • How brands measure performance, from attribution and incrementality to mix modelling

 

The Role

This is a permanent role at the heart of ClickZ. You'll run the day-to-day content engine: spotting the stories that matter to marketing leaders, turning them into sharp content across email, social and the website, and growing the audience that reads it.

The work is varied. In a single week you might cover a session at a major commerce event, publish a piece on a platform change, prepare a leadership Q&A, and review a stack of contributor pitches. You'll also build ClickZ's network of event partners, contributors, PR contacts and industry leaders, and meet many of them in person at industry events.

You'll work closely with ClickZ's lead, who sets the brand's strategy, and you'll have real ownership of your workstreams from the start. This is an office-based role in London.

This role suits someone with a journalist's instinct for a story, a marketer's eye for an audience, and the energy to keep both going every week.

 

What you'll work on

Your time will be spread across three areas, with content creation at the core. All three serve one goal: growing the ClickZ brand and getting its content to more of the right people.

Focus area What it covers
Content creation The core of the role: editorial content on market trends, event coverage, brand leadership interviews and Q&As, flagship newsletters, and social content
Audience growth and content analysis Growing ClickZ's readership and subscribers, testing new formats, and using performance data to decide what to create next
Network and community Building relationships with event partners, marketing and commerce leaders, PR teams and contributors, online and in person at industry events

 

Key Responsibilities
